editorial:
Grace just married into the Le Domas family, a wealthy clan obsessed with old traditions. On her wedding night, instead of a honeymoon, she is handed a mysterious box and told to play hide-and-seek. At first it sounds silly, but the family treats it like a deadly ritual. Grace, played by Samara Weaving, goes from nervous bride to fierce survivor as the mansion turns into a hunting ground. The movie mixes sharp humor with bloody chaos, so you are laughing one minute and gasping the next. It never takes itself too seriously, which makes the wild premise work.

The standout is Weaving, who carries every scene with charm and grit. The supporting cast is funny, especially the clueless relatives who keep messing up. Pacing is quick, with plenty of twists and gory surprises. Some jokes miss, and the ending is over the top, but that is part of the fun. If you like horror with a wink, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: Grace survives the night and learns the family curse is real. When the sun rises, the Le Domas relatives who failed to kill her begin exploding one by one. Her husband Alex tries to save her but is killed by his own family. Grace walks out covered in blood as police arrive. The final shot shows her sitting on the mansion steps, smoking and laughing, finally free from the deadly game.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves horror comedies with strong heroines.
